info.title: Pezzotflix Video Service API
info.description:
Contract-first API of the Video Service (ADR 0004). This spec is the source of truth:
the server validates against it and clients generate their types from the bundled
`dist/openapi.json`. Paths are absolute; the server registers them without a prefix.
Control plane under /video/api/v1, data plane under /video/media.
Enums are open for clients (tolerate unknown values). Changes within v1 are additive only.

tags.name: media
tags.description: Data plane; extractable into a future video-worker.

get.summary: Liveness and readiness for the container healthcheck.
GetServerInfo — name, API versions, features, ingest and provider status.
Poll notifications (ADR 0004). Without cursor returns the current position and no events.

post.summary: SelectProfile — returns the profile context token (P2). No auth in the MVP.

get.summary: GetHome — rows composed by the server (I1).
Search by localized and original title (FTS5, diacritics-insensitive).
Seasons of a series or episodes of a season, with the profile watch state.
Next episode to watch in a series for the profile.

put.summary: MarkWatched (idempotent, propagated to episodes for series/season).

post.summary: StartPlayback — the Decision Engine plans the minimum transformation and returns data-plane locators.

503.description: MEDIA_UNAVAILABLE, or STREAM_PREPARING when the file's keyframe index is not ready and needs a slow probe; the index job is moved to the front of the queue and the client shows "preparing" and retries after Retry-After (ADR 0003).

delete.summary: Terminate a session (also another profile's, to free the slot). Idempotent.

post.summary: ReportProgress — also the heartbeat. The latest client timestamp wins.
StopPlayback — closes the ViewingRecord and updates WatchState (90%). Idempotent.
ChangeTracks — may re-plan (new locators, possibly a different mode).
Client playback failure — the server re-plans from the suspect dimension with the minimum change (doc 04 §8).
post.description: The failed format stays excluded for the session. audio: one step down the audio ladder (Direct Play becomes Direct Stream with converted audio; Direct Stream stays Direct Stream with another audio format). subtitle: the next subtitle treatment; if there is none (e.g. burn-in on a 4K source), playback goes on without that track and the session reasons say why. video, container or unknown: a heavier mode (Direct Play, Direct Stream, Transcode). If the required step does not exist (4K Transcode), 422 NO_COMPATIBLE_PLAN.

get.summary: ListLibraryRoots (configured from env in the MVP).

post.summary: TriggerScan — one root or all. Idempotent while a scan is queued.
ResolveCase — link to a candidate, an existing item, or a new manual item.

get.summary: SearchProvider — manual match lookup (Wikidata, TMDB when configured).

post.summary: ExplainPlaybackDecision — Decision Engine output without starting anything.

get.summary: Direct Play — the original file bytes, with Range support.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: Multivariant playlist (main.m3u8), media playlist (media-N.m3u8), init segment (init-N.mp4) or media segment (seg-N-NNNNN.m4s); N is the rendition index.

get.summary: Direct Stream / Transcode — HLS fMP4 playlist or segment.
get.description: Segments are produced on demand. A resource listed in the playlist never answers 404 while the session is alive: if it is not ready in time the answer is 503 with Retry-After, and the client retries. 404 is only for a name that is not in the playlist; 410 once the session is closed or re-planned (new token) (ADR 0003).

500.description: STREAM_FAILED, after one automatic retry by the server. Terminal for the stream: every later data-plane request of the session answers 500 STREAM_FAILED at once; recovery is only through reportPlaybackFailure.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: Track id plus format extension, e.g. s5.vtt or s7.sup.

get.summary: Sidecar or extracted subtitle track (WebVTT for text, PGS .sup for client rendering).
get.description: While the track's availability is growing, the answer is a single streamed response without Content-Length that grows until the extraction's first pass ends; if the extraction is queued, the response stays open with no bytes until it starts. Once complete, the same url serves the whole file with Range (ADR 0003).

parameters.name: imageKey
parameters.description: Content-addressed key (hash); a changed image gets a new URL.

get.summary: GetImage — size variant (WebP). Cache policy per ADR 0004 (immutable except TMDB images).

profileToken.description: Profile context from SelectProfile (P2). Not real auth in the MVP (LAN only).

Id.description: Opaque, stable id (UUIDv7). Clients never build ids.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details with a stable machine-readable code.

type.description: library.item_added | library.item_updated | library.item_removed | ingest.progress | identification.needs_review | playback.session_terminated | playback.subtitle_ready. playback.subtitle_ready payload: { sessionId, trackId, availability } when an extracted subtitle track becomes complete; the client re-reads the track url. Extraction is per file and shared: the event is emitted for every active session on that file, each with that session's current sessionId (ADR 0003).

profileToken.description: Opaque profile context; send it as an Authorization Bearer header.

url.description: Relative URL with a size variant placeholder resolved by the server.

badges.description: Technical badges, e.g. 4K, HDR10, DV, Atmos, TrueHD.

available.description: At least one linked file is online.

query.description: ListItems parameters that reproduce this row, for "see all".

id.description: Stable track id within the file ("s3" embedded stream index, "x:<id>" sidecar).

label.description: Human summary, e.g. "4K · Dolby Vision · TrueHD 7.1 · ITA/ENG".

attributions.description: Data sources shown for this item (e.g. TMDB, Wikidata).

ClientCapabilities.description: Declared by the client (doc 03 §4.1, doc 04 §5). The server may apply per-device overrides.

model.description: Device model. The web client puts browser, version and OS here (e.g. "Firefox 159.0.1; Windows 11"), so that a server-side override (doc 03 I2) can target a browser.

audioTrackSelection.description: True if the client can choose the audio track inside a multi-track container in Direct Play. Chrome, Edge and Firefox expose audioTracks only behind a flag (MDN BCD; not probed by spike S2). Absent means false: Direct Play then needs a file with a single, supported audio track (doc 04 §4.1).

video.description: Video decoders. A browser fills this from a fixed list of codec strings probed with MediaSource.isTypeSupported (doc 03 I6). The Decision Engine compares codec, profile, bit depth and resolution, not level or tier: a level/tier rejection is caught by the stream.mimeType check and re-planned.

codec.description: Fixed vocabulary: h264 | hevc | av1 | vp9.

profiles.description: Fixed vocabulary, e.g. high (h264), main | main10 (hevc), main (av1), profile0 | profile2 (vp9). Bit depth goes in maxBitDepth.

hdr.description: HDR formats the client accepts and presents, also when it converts them itself for an SDR display (doc 04 P5): HDR10, HLG, HDR10+, DV5, DV8.1 ...

displayHdr.description: True if the display shows HDR. HDR formats in `hdr` with displayHdr false mean the client presents them itself on an SDR display; the session reason says so (doc 04 P5). It changes the reason only, not the plan. Absent means true when `hdr` is not empty (previous semantics): the plan uses `hdr` only and the reason does not claim a client-side conversion. The web client reads it from matchMedia('(dynamic-range: high)') when the session starts.

codec.description: Fixed vocabulary: aac | ac3 | eac3 | flac | opus | truehd | dts | dtshd | pcm.

maxChannels.description: Max channels the client decodes for this codec (e.g. 8 for FLAC in a browser), not the output channels; the client downmixes to its output itself (doc 04 §4.3, §5).

switchWithoutRestart.description: About the stream only: true when the client can switch to this track without restarting the stream, e.g. any client_render or sidecar track that has a url. Extraction state is in availability, not here (ADR 0003, doc 04 §6.3).

delivery.description: embedded: inside the stream; sidecar: text track served separately (WebVTT); burned: in the video (Transcode only); client_render: image track (.sup) served separately for a client-side renderer (doc 04 P3). Never attach a client_render track as a text <track>.

url.description: Data-plane locator for sidecar or client-rendered subtitles.

availability.description: Subtitle tracks served separately (sidecar, client_render) only. growing: extraction is running and the url streams a response that grows until the first pass ends; it may not yet cover the part of the film before the session start. complete: the url serves the whole file with Range. The client learns of the change from the playback.subtitle_ready event and then re-reads the url. If the extraction is queued and not started yet, the url keeps the response open with no bytes until it starts (ADR 0003).

reasons.description: Human-readable reasons for the chosen mode (doc 04 §3).

url.description: Data-plane locator (relative). Never build it client-side.

mimeType.description: MIME type with the RFC 6381 `codecs` parameter of the exact streams, e.g. 'video/mp4; codecs="hvc1.2.4.L153.B0, flac"'. For hls-fmp4 it is the type of the media segments, not of the playlist. A browser checks it with MediaSource.isTypeSupported (canPlayType for progressive) before starting the player; if false it calls reportPlaybackFailure with error MIME_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED and the suspect dimension (doc 03 I6).

startOffsetMs.description: Always 0 for every protocol in v1: the progressive file and the hls-fmp4 VOD playlist both cover the whole film, and the player seeks to resumePositionMs (ADR 0003).

mediaTimestampOffsetMs.description: Constant offset added to the original timeline (PTS - start_time of the file) in the media timestamps: 10000 for hls-fmp4, 0 for progressive; absent means 0. For progressive the offset is simply 0. For hls-fmp4 only, hls.js adds its own shift from the first loaded fragment, so the client computes timelineOffsetMs = initPTS * 1000 / timescale - mediaTimestampOffsetMs at every INIT_PTS_FOUND and uses original time = currentTime + timelineOffsetMs, both for positions and subtitles and, inverted, for seeks to an original time (ADR 0003, ADR 0005).

bitrate.description: Estimated bitrates of the stream as served, for the client's buffer limits (MSE quotas). The same peak and average appear as BANDWIDTH and AVERAGE-BANDWIDTH in the hls-fmp4 multivariant playlist.

peakBps.description: Peak over one segment (hls-fmp4) or over the file.

audioBps.description: Selected audio track alone (separate MSE audio quota).

clientTs.description: Client clock in ms; the latest wins.

error.description: Player error, e.g. MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED. Client vocabulary also includes MIME_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED (stream.mimeType rejected by isTypeSupported or canPlayType before starting) and STREAM_FAILED (a data-plane 5xx that stayed fatal after the player's own retries; send suspect unknown, the server re-plans from its own record of the failure, doc 04 §8).

files.description: Count of media files per state.

allowedResolutions.description: multi_part and disc_structure allow only ignore (library standard §7.1).

actions.description: Per dimension: container, video, audio, subtitles → none | remux | convert:<codec> | transcode | burn_in

Retry-After.description: Seconds before retrying. Advisory; hls.js ignores it and uses its own backoff.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page (nextCursor).

SessionToken.name: sessionToken
SessionToken.description: Session token (P9). Never logged in clear.
